title: Cost-Effective Payment Gateway for Startups in India: Razorpay Costs Over the First 90 Days
summary: Plan your startup’s first 90 days with Razorpay. Compare setup fees, AMC, transaction charges, GST and welcome-offer limits using worked examples.
body_markdown:
A cost-effective payment gateway for a startup is one whose total payment-collection cost fits its sales volume, payment methods and operating needs, with fixed charges and introductory discounts clearly separated.


For illustration, consider a startup collecting Rs 50,000 a month. The founder needs to know how much remains after payment costs. What will payment collection cost over the first 90 days, and what changes afterwards?


Zero setup fees, no annual maintenance charge (AMC), zero MDR and a conditional platform-fee waiver describe different things. A zero-AMC plan can still carry processing charges, taxes and optional service costs. Compare those amounts over the same period using the payment methods your customers will use.


This guide explains Razorpay’s standard cost structure, the conditions of its 90-day offer, worked budgets for low-volume startups in India, and the normal-price costs to plan for when introductory credits stop applying.


## Key Takeaways


- **Compare costs in rupees at your expected sales volume.** Small differences in transaction rates can produce modest savings when collections are low. For example, a hypothetical 0.25-percentage-point rate difference on Rs 50,000 of monthly collections equals Rs 125 before tax. Include fixed charges over the same comparison period to understand the actual difference.
- **Build separate budgets for launch and normal pricing.** Estimate your first 90 days using expected successful collections and payment methods, then calculate costs after introductory benefits end. Starting with normal pricing gives your startup a usable forecast even if it does not qualify for an offer or exhausts its credits earlier than expected.
- **Razorpay’s 90-day welcome offer can reduce eligible platform fees.** Eligible new Razorpay merchants can receive amount credits covering up to Rs 5 lakh of cumulative eligible domestic payments for 90 days from account activation, whichever limit comes first. Onboarding requirements, payment-method exclusions, and fair-usage conditions apply. Review[Razorpay’s official offer terms](https://razorpay.com/terms/90-day-free-pg-offer/) before budgeting.
- **Check the remaining credit balance against each payment.** Low total collections do not guarantee that every transaction is covered. If an individual payment exceeds the remaining amount-credit balance, fees can apply to its entire value. Check both the balance and expiry date using Razorpay’s[credits documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/credits/) .
- **Keep taxes and additional charges visible.** Zero setup fees and zero AMC do not mean zero total payment costs. The offer does not waive applicable statutory levies, and a KYC processing fee of Rs 199 plus tax may apply. Confirm invoice treatment and separately priced services under the[offer terms](https://razorpay.com/terms/90-day-free-pg-offer/) .
- **Assess operational value alongside billed fees.** Track integration effort, reconciliation time, failed payments and recovered collections using your own business data. Choose the payment flow your startup needs today, and add optional services when their value justifies their cost. The most affordable setup depends on your payment mix, sales volume and operating requirements.


## What Makes a Payment Gateway Cost-Effective for a Low-Volume Startup?


For a low-volume startup, a cost-effective payment gateway combines manageable fixed charges with clearly disclosed transaction costs and tools that fit the way it sells. Compare the total cost over the same period, including taxes and optional services. A low percentage fee alone cannot establish the cheapest choice.


In this article, “low volume” means Rs 25,000 to Rs 2,00,000 in monthly successful collections. That is an editorial planning range for the worked examples below, not an official pricing tier.


### Start With Fixed Costs, Then Compare Variable Charges


A setup fee is a possible one-time charge to open an account. An annual maintenance charge, or AMC, is a recurring yearly charge. A platform fee is a usage charge tied to transactions. These are distinct line items, and not every merchant pays every one of them.


Compare both setups over the same 90-day launch window. On Rs 50,000 of successful collections each month, a hypothetical 0.25-percentage-point rate saving is Rs 125 a month, or Rs 375 over 90 days, before tax. If that lower-rate setup also requires a Rs 1,000 annual fee paid at launch, the fixed cash outflow exceeds those 90-day savings by Rs 625. These figures are illustrative.


There is also a cash-timing point. An annual fee billed at launch is a full cash outflow in that quarter, even if your management accounts amortise it across twelve months. For a startup watching runway, the cash date is the one that hurts.


### Match the Gateway to How You Actually Collect Money


One-off service payments, a hosted checkout and recurring billing are different workflows with different operational demands. Pick the flow before you pick the fee.


Before comparing anything, write down your expected monthly successful collections, average ticket size, payment-method mix, refund profile and any optional products you genuinely need. A hundred Rs 200 payments and two Rs 10,000 payments both total Rs 20,000. At the same percentage rate and payment method, their base processing fee is identical. Transaction count matters separately when flat per-transaction charges or operational work apply.


Payment failures and developer time are real operational considerations. They need your own data, and they belong beside the billed processing-fee total rather than inside it.


> **DID YOU KNOW:** A 0.25-percentage-point rate difference equals Rs 125 on Rs 50,000. Use absolute rupees, not percentages, to judge whether a feature or a fixed charge is worth paying for.


## Does Razorpay Have Zero Setup Fees and Zero Annual Maintenance Charges?


Razorpay’s standard Payment Gateway pricing lists no setup charge and no annual maintenance charge. These fixed-fee terms are separate from processing fees and from any conditional introductory offer. Confirm the applicable payment-method rate and optional services for your account on the[official pricing page](https://razorpay.com/pricing/) .


### Standard Payment Gateway Terms and Startup Benefits


Razorpay lists zero setup fees and zero AMC in its standard Payment Gateway pricing. The public pricing page does not list DPIIT recognition as a condition for those fixed-fee terms. Special startup benefit programmes have their own eligibility requirements.


Merchant onboarding and KYC are a separate track from any funded-startup benefit programme. Startup registration on its own does not guarantee activation, credits or negotiated rates.


A KYC processing charge is also a separately disclosed item. Zero setup fee should not be read as a promise that every activation-related charge is zero.


### What a Zero-AMC Label Does Not Cover


Zero AMC describes one field on a rate card. These still need their own budget lines:


- Transaction and platform fees on successful payments
- Applicable taxes on those fees
- Developer time or third-party commerce-platform transaction charges
- Any service you separately choose to enable


Also keep the scope tight. Payment Gateway pricing does not extend to a physical terminal, a banking product, a payroll subscription or every product in the suite. For a wider view, see our guide to a[payment gateway with no hidden charges](https://razorpay.com/blog/payment-gateway-transparent-pricing-explained/) .


> **PRO-TIP:** Keep your account’s accepted commercial schedule open beside the public pricing page. If the scope differs, get written clarification before you finalise the budget.


## How the Razorpay First-90-Day Offer Changes Your Cost


Evaluate the welcome offer as a reduction in eligible platform fees, then calculate the other payable lines separately. Your budget needs two cases: eligible transactions while credits remain, and chargeable transactions after expiry, exclusion, or a credit-balance limit. Confirm your account’s tax treatment before quoting an all-in rupee saving.


### Offer Eligibility, Time Limit and Exclusions


The following conditions summarise the[official offer terms:](https://razorpay.com/terms/90-day-free-pg-offer/)


- Qualifying new merchants complete KYC and receive activation on or after 1 July 2026. The benefit covers up to Rs 5,00,000 of cumulative domestic payment value for 90 days from activation, ending at whichever limit is reached first.
- International payments, prepaid cards, corporate credit cards, American Express, Diners Club, and all EMI-based methods are excluded. One redemption applies per PAN or bank account, and the first activated MID qualifies. Merchants who transacted previously are excluded.
- Taxes and statutory levies on platform fees remain applicable. A KYC processing fee of Rs 199 plus applicable taxes may be charged, subject to verification of business documents. Unused credits expire with the window. If credit card transactions exceed 90% of processed volume, the fair-usage clause allows withdrawal of the offer and retrospective standard charges from the date of detection.


Read “Rs 5 lakh” correctly. It is payment-value eligibility, not Rs 5 lakh of cash, not a monthly allowance, and not a fee balance. It is also not three calendar billing months. Standard platform fees resume automatically at the applicable endpoint.


### Watch the Individual Transaction, Not Just the Cumulative Total


The[credits documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/dashboard/account-settings/credits/) explains that a transaction exceeding the available amount credit can attract fees on its entire value, with credits not applied partially. Subtracting Rs 5 lakh from total GMV can therefore misstate your fees.


**Worked illustration.** Suppose Rs 10,000 of credit remains and a Rs 15,000 eligible payment arrives. Because the payment exceeds the balance, the fee can apply to the full Rs 15,000. At an assumed 2% rate, that is Rs 300 before GST, not Rs 100 on the Rs 5,000 difference.

Confirm your account’s credit ledger before assuming either outcome.


> **PRO-TIP:** Check credit history and expiry before launch, and again before any unusually large payment. Do not split transactions artificially to work around offer conditions.


## What Would Razorpay Cost Over Your First 90 Days?


Estimate 90-day payment costs from successful collections by payment method, then add applicable taxes and separate charges. Calculate the standard-price case first. For an eligible introductory offer, apply credits transaction by transaction and keep taxes, possible KYC charges, and optional services outside the platform-fee saving.


### Standard-Price Budget for Four Low-Volume Scenarios


**Assumptions:** three consecutive 30-day planning periods; monthly successful collections remain constant; all modelled payments use an applicable 2% platform rate; GST is illustrated at 18% of that fee. No introductory credits, refunds, disputes, method-specific charges, KYC charge, third-party fees, or optional services are included. These are calculations, not account quotes. Confirm the rate that applies to you using the[Razorpay payment gateway pricing explainer](https://razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-payment-gateway-pricing-explained/) .

The final column is deliberately a scoped subtotal. It is not an all-in startup cost, and the 2.36% implied by these assumptions is not an MDR figure. The 2% assumption does not apply to every payment method or optional product.


Notice what the first row tells a bootstrapped founder. At Rs 25,000 a month, the modelled 90-day fee-and-tax subtotal is Rs 1,770. At that scale, the size of any fixed annual commitment usually matters more than a fractional rate difference.

## Which Costs Should You Keep Outside the Headline Gateway Rate?


Keep processing charges, statutory taxes, refunds, disputes, optional products and your own operating costs as separate budget lines. Some may be zero or inapplicable to you. Check the account agreement and your invoices before filling in the worksheet. This gives a clearer forecast than treating a zero-AMC label as the full price.


### GST, Refunds and Chargebacks


GST applies to the fee, not to the sale. On a Rs 1,000 collection at an assumed 2% rate, the platform fee is Rs 20 and GST at 18% of that fee is Rs 3.60. The[pricing explainer](https://razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-payment-gateway-pricing-explained/) sets out this treatment. Never apply GST to the entire sale value inside a gateway-fee calculation.


Returning a customer’s money and reversing the original processing charge are two different events. Our explainer on[whether MDR comes back on refunds](https://razorpay.com/blog/do-you-get-mdr-back-on-refunds/) walks through how transaction state affects this. Verify the current account-specific refund and tax-reversal treatment rather than assuming all refund costs are free.


If disputes are relevant to your category, use the dispute and representment charges in your merchant agreement when building the budget. Keep actual dispute costs separate from your ordinary processing-fee forecast.


### Optional Features and Third-Party Costs


Instant settlements, recurring billing, specific payment methods, and other added services each need their own rate and applicability check before you enable them.


Hosting, development work, commerce-platform transaction charges and accounting labour are separate from Razorpay’s Payment Gateway setup and AMC fields. A commerce platform may levy its own transaction fee on top of whatever your gateway charges, which belongs in a different budget row.


Keep this practical. Tag every item as “needed now”, “optional later” or “not relevant”.


Settlement timing deserves a line too, though it is not a fee. The[settlements FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/settlements/faqs/) describes a standard domestic settlement cycle of T+2 working days, where T is the payment capture date, subject to bank approval and account factors. Working days exclude second and fourth Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays. Confirm the cycle applicable to your account. Track expected settlement dates in your cash-flow sheet, separately from charges.


## How Can a Founder Keep Launch Costs Proportionate to Sales?


Choose the payment flow that fits your first customers. A payment link can suit an individual collection, a hosted page can suit a small campaign or service, and a website checkout can suit an online store. Compare the operational work and relevant charges before adding more products.


### Start With the Collection Flow You Need


- **[Payment Links](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) :** share a collection link through a business channel your customer already uses. Check which link-related features are included for your account.
- **[Payment Pages](https://razorpay.com/payment-pages/) :** supports a hosted collection page without coding or building a separate website, which suits an early launch or a single campaign.
- **[Payment Gateway](https://razorpay.com/payment-gateway/) :** connect your website or app checkout. Keep custom development and any plugin or platform cost in a separate budget row.


Consider recurring billing only if your startup genuinely needs repeat collections, and check its separate pricing before enabling it. Payroll, lending and banking products are not part of the Payment Gateway cost question.


### Use Your Own Payment Data to Judge Value


Track first-attempt failures, eventually recovered payments and successful collections as three separate figures. Each tells you something different about your checkout.


More revenue collected is not automatically profit or a fee saving. Use your own completed and recovered payment data, together with the cost of operating your checkout, to assess value. For a broader selection framework beyond costing, our[low-cost payment gateway decision guide](https://razorpay.com/blog/low-cost-payment-gateway-in-india-the-complete-decision-guide/) covers it.


## What Happens After Day 90, or When Credits Stop Applying?


Switch the forecast to the applicable normal rate as soon as introductory credits stop covering a transaction. Review next month’s expected sales by method, add taxes and any enabled products, then compare that ongoing cost with your margin. The offer period should never be your only affordability test.


### Rebuild the Month-Four Budget


Take an illustrative Rs 1,00,000 of successful collections at an assumed 2% platform fee. That is Rs 2,000 in fees plus Rs 360 GST at 18% of the fee, a Rs 2,360 subtotal before any other applicable lines. Not every account or payment method uses this rate, so substitute your own.


The fixed-fee scope established earlier does not change at day 91. The end of a platform-fee promotion does not, by itself, create an annual maintenance charge.


Recheck your commercial schedule as volume or payment mix shifts. A custom-pricing enquiry is a discussion you can open, not a guaranteed reduction.


> **PRO-TIP:** Set a calendar reminder before the 90-day offer expiry date, and check remaining credits sooner if volume grows faster than planned. Keep a normal-price budget from day one.


## How to Build Your Startup’s 90-Day Payment Budget


1. Write down your activation date, your account commercial schedule and your expected 90-day selling window.
2. Estimate successful collections and transaction count for each 30-day period, split by payment method.
3. List fixed provider charges separately from development, hosting and third-party platform costs.
4. Calculate the normal platform and method fees using the rates that apply to your account.
5. Check offer eligibility and remaining credits payment by payment, keeping excluded or oversized transactions in the chargeable column.
6. Add invoice-confirmed taxes, any KYC charge and only the optional services you intend to use.
7. At the end of each period, reconcile five artefacts: the payments report, the fee line items, the amount credit history, the GST invoice and the settlement reconciliation report. Record operational effort in its own column.
8. Prepare your first normal-price month before credits expire, then review whether the flow still fits your sales pattern and margin.


Your completed worksheet should show launch-period costs and the first month at normal pricing. Compare both with your margins before choosing a payment setup.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Razorpay a cost-effective payment gateway for a startup with low transaction volumes?


Razorpay can suit a startup that wants a standard Payment Gateway account without setup or annual maintenance charges. Check the actual transaction rates, payment flow and optional products against your expected sales. Use the standard-budget examples above and your confirmed offer eligibility to compare total costs over the same period.


### Does Razorpay charge an annual maintenance fee for small businesses?


The standard Payment Gateway pricing lists zero AMC. That does not remove processing charges, applicable tax or the price of separately enabled services. Check the current pricing and your accepted commercial schedule. Do not apply a fee quoted for another product or an older plan to the standard Payment Gateway account.


### Does a registered startup need a special plan to get zero setup fee and zero AMC?


The public Payment Gateway pricing describes those fixed-fee terms as part of the standard offering. It does not establish that DPIIT recognition is required to access them. Special startup benefit programmes carry separate eligibility, and merchant activation still depends on the relevant onboarding and verification requirements.


### Does a zero-platform-fee offer mean my first 90 days cost nothing?


No. The offer affects eligible platform fees within its stated conditions. Taxes, any applicable KYC charge, excluded payment methods and optional services need separate treatment. Use the eligibility block and the transaction-level credits example above, then confirm the final payable amount from your account invoices.


### How should I budget once the first-90-day benefit ends?


Use the normal rate for your account and payment-method mix, then add applicable taxes and any extra services. At an illustrative 2% fee and 18% GST on that fee, Rs 1,00,000 in successful collections gives a Rs 2,360 processing-and-tax subtotal. Other applicable costs remain separate lines.
